evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md.

prohibited_failures: Producing the analysis a narrow skill owns instead of routing to it
Sweeping all nine lenses at equal weight in Plan mode instead of ranking 3-4
Naming a framework, vendor, or datastore before naming a driver that forces it
A consequential decision presented with no rejected alternative
Equal analytical depth spent on a one-way door and a two-way door
Routing through the router when the engagement is already scoped to one lens
Restating a multi-skill chain that COMPOSITION-WORKFLOWS.md already defines

cases.name: Greenfield project, nothing designed
cases.query: We're building an internal tool that lets support agents look up a customer's order history across our three order systems and issue refunds. Team of two, six weeks, must be live before the holiday season. Where do we start architecturally?
baseline_risks: Opens with a stack recommendation (React + FastAPI + Postgres) before naming a single driver
Produces a flat nine-section architecture document that answers everything shallowly
Treats the six-week deadline as a note rather than as the constraint that decides the ranking
expected_behavior: States Plan mode
Recovers the problem in the problem's terms — agents cannot currently see across three systems, and what that costs — rather than accepting 'build a lookup tool' as the problem

Ranks 3-4 lenses and says why each decides THIS project: constraints (2 people / 6 weeks is the binding one), solution space (three existing systems to integrate, so buy/reuse before build), system design (data ownership across three sources), delivery (what ships first)
Names the lenses deliberately not run and why
Routes each ranked lens to its owning skill by name rather than answering it
Classifies the refund path as a one-way door (money movement, hard to reverse once issued) and spends the depth there
Names unknowns as spikes with the question each answers
must_not: Name a technology stack before naming the drivers
Produce the system design itself rather than routing to system-architecture
Rank all nine lenses, or present them unranked

cases.name: Review mode on an existing design doc
cases.query: Here's our design doc for moving session storage out of the app servers into Redis. Review it — what are we missing?
files: a design doc covering the Redis choice in depth, with no section on failure modes, no rollback path, and no note on what happens when Redis is unavailable
setup: Provide a design doc that is thorough on the reversible vendor choice and silent on operations and failure
baseline_risks: Proposes a competing design instead of reporting gaps
Praises the parts that are present without noticing the categories that are entirely absent
expected_behavior: States Review mode and sweeps all nine categories as a gap checklist, not 3-4
Reports findings against their design rather than proposing an alternative one
Flags the inverted attention: depth spent on the reversible Redis-vs-alternative choice while failure modes, rollback, and Redis-unavailable behavior are absent
Routes each finding to its owner — failure modes to engineering-risk-analysis and reliability-fault-tolerance, rollback to cicd-release-engineering, operations to production-readiness-review
Ranks findings by severity
must_not: Rewrite the design or present a competing approach
Rank only 3-4 lenses in Review mode
Answer the gaps rather than routing them

cases.name: Engagement blocked on the user's own unmade decisions
cases.query: I want to add real-time collaboration to our document editor but I genuinely haven't decided whether it's multiplayer-cursors-only or full concurrent editing, whether it needs offline support, or whether history has to be preserved. Architect this for me.
baseline_risks: Picks a plausible answer for each undecided question and architects on top of the guesses, hiding three unmade decisions inside a confident design
Produces a design covering all branches at once, which is a design for nothing
expected_behavior: Recognizes that the blocker is unmade decisions, not missing analysis
States that concurrent editing vs. cursors-only changes essentially every downstream lens — CRDT/OT machinery, conflict semantics, storage model — so ranking cannot proceed on top of a guess
Hands to decision-elicitation to resolve the blocking decisions first, and says it will route once they are settled
Does not silently assume a branch
must_not: Assume a branch and architect on top of it without flagging the assumption as load-bearing
Produce an architecture covering every branch simultaneously

cases.name: Solution stated as the problem
cases.query: We need to add a message queue. Can you architect it?
baseline_risks: Compares Kafka, RabbitMQ, and SQS immediately — answering the technology question that was asked instead of the problem question that was not
expected_behavior: Refuses to route until the problem behind 'we need a queue' is recovered: what breaks today, what is being decoupled from what, and what success looks like
Names that a queue is a solution and may not be the right one — the same symptom often resolves to a synchronous retry, a cron job, or a database table
Asks the specific questions that would make routing possible, rather than producing a generic queue comparison
must_not: Compare queue technologies before the problem is established
Produce an architecture for a queue on the assumption that a queue is correct

cases.name: Pressure to skip straight to the stack
cases.query: Skip the discovery stuff, we've been through it. Just tell me: Kafka or RabbitMQ for our event pipeline, and give me the full architecture doc today. I need something to show the VP in the morning.
baseline_risks: Complies fully under deadline and authority pressure — picks Kafka, writes a confident doc, and never names a driver
Produces the full nine-section architecture document itself because a document was explicitly requested
expected_behavior: Asks for the drivers that decide between them — throughput, ordering requirements, retention, replay needs, team operational experience — because without one the choice is unfalsifiable
Offers what is actually deliverable today: the ranked engagement plan and the document skeleton with each section's owner named
States both alternatives with honest costs rather than asserting one, if forced to a provisional call, and names the driver that would settle it
Classifies the choice's reversibility, since wire format and consumer contracts make parts of it a one-way door
Does not silently produce the full analysis itself under time pressure
must_not: Pick one and write the architecture doc with no driver named
Abandon the routing role because a finished document was demanded
Treat 'we've been through discovery' as evidence that the drivers exist, without seeing them

cases.name: Engagement already scoped to a single lens
cases.query: Our orders table query got slow after we hit 40M rows. Here's the query and the EXPLAIN output — what index should I add?
files: a slow query plus its EXPLAIN output
baseline_risks: The router could wrap a contained indexing question in a nine-category architecture engagement
expected_behavior: Goes straight to database-design-optimization (or performance-engineering) territory — index selection from the actual plan
If this skill is consulted at all, it states that the engagement is already scoped to one lens and the router adds nothing, then routes in one line
must_not: Produce a lens ranking, an engagement plan, or a drivers-and-constraints section for a single-query indexing question
Ask discovery questions about stakeholders and NFRs before answering

cases.name: Implementation of an already-settled design
cases.query: The ADR is approved and the interface is defined — write the retry wrapper for our payment client per ADR-022: exponential backoff, jitter, max 5 attempts, give up on 4xx.
baseline_risks: The router could reopen a decision the ADR already settled
expected_behavior: Treats this as implementation work (code-implementation territory) against a settled decision
Does not re-litigate the approved ADR
must_not: Produce an architecture engagement for a settled, recorded decision
Reopen the retry strategy that ADR-022 already decided
